title: Stage 57 shifted four-prime correlations
evidence_status: Finite computational observation; no universal coverage proof is claimed

definitions.residual_set: H = {N integer: N >= 4, N even, N-1 composite, N/2 composite}
definitions.representation_count: R(N) = #{(p,q): p<q, p and q prime, p+q=N}
definitions.wheel_factor: A_210(N) = product over ell in {2,3,5,7} of (ell-1 if ell divides N, otherwise ell-2)
definitions.shift: M=N+2h, h in {1,...,10}; count ordered choices from P_N x P_M

arithmetic_and_software.exactness: Integer counts and fractions.Fraction; no floating-point arithmetic in the computation or comparison

independent_methods.method_1: Trial-division primality tests; explicit p<q pair lists; Cartesian product classified by shared positions
independent_methods.method_2: Sieve of Eratosthenes; direct nested scans over lower summands p and r; candidate sums checked with prime flags and classified by equality positions
independent_methods.verification: verify_stage57.py independently reloads the saved JSON, rebuilds sieve and direct modulo-210 counts, then rechecks every row, category, normalized term, and shift aggregate

limitations: Finite computation only through N=2000 and h=1,...,10.
A_210 is a local admissibility count and gives no prime-pair error term.
The exact correlation expansion contains the prime-pair counts themselves and is not an independent analytic lower bound.
No theorem proving R(N)>0 for every N in H has been supplied.
